body:
The finer-summary candidate is still **unqualified**. Both fresh component processes show a slowdown against actual Native68 at every captured 33K–126K shape. Stage timing identifies the mean scorer as the main cost. Removing a compiler-generated barrier per loaded summary row preserves all tested score bits and passes cache/graph/lifecycle and strict initialization checks, but still loses native speed. All unfavorable runs are retained. A contiguous page-copy loading screen is in progress; no new model-quality or request-speed claim is made. [Current optimization and receipts](experiments/2026-11-05-block-load/README.md).

The latest candidate replaces iterative 64-key clustering with means of native 8-key blocks, while retaining native fine-score arithmetic and the same fine-scored candidate budget. The implementation and strict no-loss final-answer gate are prepared; **it has not yet established a request-speed win or completed-answer quality for this new representation**. All experiments remain unpromoted.

The finer summaries substantially improve native-key overlap on the reused diagnostic capture (+7.3 to +15.6 percentage points), which is a selection proxy, not an answer-quality result. Six graph/cache/lifecycle cases, all 12 actual-input batches, and strict initialization checks pass; the sanitizer reports zero errors. Runtime performs no clustering, reference scoring, grading or host activation copies. Component timing and final-answer evaluation are the next gates. [Implementation and all receipts](experiments/2026-11-05-block-summary/README.md).

The actual native control retains its 68-byte/key cache layout; the candidate pays for 100 bytes/key, summary construction and updates. This prevents common padding from concealing cache/admission cost. Server speculation/prefill/decode counters are collected outside request timers. New wrong or incomplete answers where matched native succeeds reject a candidate; independent benchmark keys and executable tests judge final content. A 65,536-token allowance, temperature0, seed0 and high-effort thinking are shared.

Native indexer selection scans the visible key cache for each query. This draft adds a TileLang page-centroid shortlist, direct candidate assembly and cache-owned summaries, with independent completed-answer evaluation. The target is better final-answer quality and useful request performance. Thinking may diverge. Promoted configuration and immutable release evidence remain unchanged.

The completed dense-only LongBench v2 pilot allows **65,536 generated tokens** on both arms, temperature 0, seed 0 and high-effort thinking. All 48 responses end naturally with completed final content. Two fresh boots per arm produce:

| Arm | Correct / 12 independent documents | Total request time, two boots |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native C36 | 8 / 12, both boots | 631.35 / 631.42 s |
| Dense LSA, native source | 9 / 12, both boots | 654.01 / 654.54 s |

LSA gains one independently correct answer and loses none in every boot pairing. Its total request time is **3.6% higher**. Correct completed answers per second is 8.56% higher in this pilot; that is a useful-throughput measure, not a lower-latency claim. One discordant document gives paired p=0.5, so general quality superiority is not established. Repeated boots do not increase the quality sample beyond 12. The frozen 45-document, document-disjoint held-out set remains unseen. Full uncertainty and limitations are in [results](experiments/2026-11-05-answer-quality/results.md) and [all raw receipts](experiments/2026-11-05-answer-quality/runs/pilot-window-02/).

Increasing the allowance resolves a real completion failure: the previously truncated table question now finishes correctly after 23,999 tokens on native and 23,838 on LSA. Both reproduce this on their repeat boot. The former 8192-token cohort was cancelled at the owner's request, restored normally and retained separately; its settings are not mixed with this comparison.

**This remains unqualified for promotion.** The wider source-1024 operating point is complete and **rejected**. Both fresh boots score 8/12 in 1126.13 / 1126.42 seconds, about 78% slower than native. Each reaches 65,536 thinking tokens without final content on the table question. This is an incomplete answer, not an incorrect completed final answer. The repeated run and all conditions are retained in [source-1024 receipts](experiments/2026-11-05-answer-quality/runs/pilot-window-03/). The same-day native controls are reused only after the strict identical-input/source guard passes. C37 restoration and independent all-node verification pass.

Native operand collection on three disjoint public source documents is complete, followed by exact native replay of all 768 captured rank-0 query rows. Four query-weighted maps are fitted out of band on only the two fitting documents; the separate validation document retains 60.7–66.6% of query-direction energy. No benchmark questions or answers supply fitting data. Actual selection validation is complete on the separate document: dense native-key overlap changes by +0.12 to +0.46 percentage points, while source-block overlap falls by 0.46 points. With slower construction, this fixed-32D probe does not justify serving integration. It has no completed-answer or request-speed qualification. All diagnostic failures and clean releases are retained in [the fitting experiment](experiments/2026-11-05-selector-fitting/README.md). The projected-summary kernel passes synthetic correctness and strict initialization checks, but its two-process construction timings are slower. No fitted map is in serving and no learned-selector quality or request-speed claim is made.

Implementation details relevant to review:

- The earlier serving pilots use balanced 64-key cluster summaries on completed physical pages. Partial visible pages remain directly scored; metadata follows prefix reuse and page recycling.
- Direct assembly reads selected pages, retains ordered candidates/counts/padding and applies native MXFP4 fine scoring to each retained key once. The earlier pilot reserves 73 bytes/key in both arms; the new full-model comparison uses actual native68 versus block8 layout100.
- A 256-row prefill workspace and covered-domain paths reduce launch overhead. Necessary summary construction and updates remain inside request timing.
- The timed implementation runs no native reference, exclusion-proof bounds, duplicate validation scoring, output comparison, grading or host activation copies.
- The earlier candidate uses unlearned page centroids; the latest candidate uses means per 8-key block. Separate native operand capture and out-of-band query-weighted metric fitting are complete; the completed key-retention proxy does not justify integrating the fixed-32D probe. No fitted map has run in serving, and no learned-selector result is claimed.

The independent benchmark pins official code, dataset, tokenizer, prompts, answer extractor and input hashes. Only final content is graded against the benchmark key; native output is not an oracle. All reasoning and unsuccessful attempts count toward elapsed time. HumanEvalPlus executable grading is prepared and self-checked separately; no model coding result is claimed.

Validation includes fresh application of the scratch guard plus four LSA patches against C36 with six mounted sources verified byte-for-byte; ten raw-token-client tests and eight independent oracle/selection tests; mechanical cache/graph/lifecycle checks; source-1024 retained-score/source-handoff checks; separate native 64-row capture replay and zero-error strict initcheck; named/default doctor; and diff checks. Earlier compiler, fidelity and unfavorable performance runs are retained. No image build is claimed.

The complete pilot runs without memory-guard events, swap growth or thermal slowdown (minimum available memory 7.11 GiB). Tracked C37 is restored once at 2026-11-05 10:59:32 UTC and independently verified on all three Spaceport nodes: expected image, clean checkouts, no experimental mounts/environment and all reservations removed. The later native collection also restores C37, independently verified at 2026-11-05 12:16:24 UTC on all three nodes. Generated text, token IDs, activations and fitted weights remain node-local.

Historical fixed-128-token request screens show 8–14% higher aggressive cached throughput in point estimates, with several two-boot intervals including no gain. They stop inside reasoning and do not qualify completed answers. Their full runs and failures remain in [request results](experiments/2026-11-04-token-lsa/paged/request-results.md).

The final standalone validation releases sp8 at 2026-11-05 12:53:46 UTC; independent verification confirms no reservation, container or GPU process and a clean published checkout. No fitted map is in the timed runtime. The larger 65,536-token evaluation allowance remains unchanged.

A further out-of-band variance-margin probe exactly reproduces the original selection at zero margin. A coefficient selected only on the two fitting documents improves native-selection overlap by 0.13–0.59 percentage points on the reused diagnostic document. This establishes neither final-answer superiority nor request speed, and no margin is added to serving. All grid values and allocator/release observations are retained in [the variance screen](experiments/2026-11-05-variance-shortlist/README.md).
title: Develop TileLang LSA with independent answer-quality evaluation
